Watch this kettle get loud, then go quieter.
That roar means your kettle isn't boiling yet.
Here's why. The water touching the hot element boils first, into tiny bubbles of steam.
But the water above it is cooler, so each bubble rises, cools, and collapses back into water.
All those tiny collapses, ringing through the kettle: that's the roar.
Once all the water is near 100 degrees, the bubbles survive to the top and pop gently.
So the roar means not yet. The quieter bubbling is the boil, right before the click.
